authority_rule: The original published study is the only source of truth. Every claim scored must trace to one of this study's primary_sources, with a page, table or figure reference. If a finding in this registry is not supported by the source, mark it not_testable with reason claim_not_in_any_source and say so; the registry can be wrong, the study cannot.

primary_sources.cite: Carroll et al., PLOS Genetics 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1002117

replication_targets.finding: Group X (S106P, L111Q) is the adaptive, function-switching pair. Introduced into AncGR1 it recapitulates a large portion of the AncGR1-to-AncGR2 shift: EC50 rises 169-fold for aldosterone and 57-fold for DOC, but only 2-fold for cortisol. The pair is internally epistatic -- L111Q alone has little effect on sensitivity to any hormone, S106P alone dramatically reduces activation by all ligands, and only the combination switches preference. Mechanism: S106P kinks the backbone and partially unwinds helix 7, repositioning site 111 so L111Q can hydrogen-bond cortisol's C17-hydroxyl. Ortlund names this conformational epistasis. Figure 2A depicts L111Q followed by S106P as the probable path through functional intermediates; S106P first greatly reduces ligand sensitivity. This supports a preferred path, not directly observed historical chronology.
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon rank sites 106 and 111 as a coupled pair, above the background pairing rate?

replication_targets.finding: Group Z (N26T, Q105L) is permissive for group Y. Both are required. Adding Z in the absence of Y has little or no effect on ligand-activated transcription -- the signature of a permissive substitution. Structurally, N26T adds a hydrogen bond between helix 3 and the AF-H loop, and Q105L lets helix 7 pack more tightly against helix 3. Separately, Y27R (from the earlier AncCR-to-AncGR1 interval) is also permissive: reversing it in the GR-like AncGR1+X+Y+Z abolishes activation by all ligands, while introducing it into AncCR or AncGR1 has negligible effect.
replication_targets.test: Recall of the permissive sites 26 and 105 (and 27) among epistaeon's detected partners of the group X and group Y sites. Note these are functionally silent on their own backgrounds, so a method keyed to phenotypic effect size would be expected to miss them.

replication_targets.finding: Direct reversal of X is impaired in AncGR2: AncGR2-x and all tested reversals restoring x without reversing the restrictive group W lose activation. Group W is H84Q, Y91C, A107Y, G114Q and L197M. Reversing W in the AncGR2-xyz background substantially restores ancestral promiscuous hormone response; individual Y107A or the interacting pairs Q84H/C91Y and Q114G/M197L partially rescue it. Reversing W alone does not switch the derived receptor to the ancestral phenotype. The experiments establish conditional paths for reversal, not an absolute inability to reverse and not the chronology of every individual substitution.
replication_targets.source: Bridgham 2009, Fig. 1f-1g, Fig. 2a-2c, Fig. 3a-3b, Fig. 4a-4b and accompanying text (pp. 516-518)
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon recover the tested group-level conditional constraint: reversing W (and Y for ancestral-conformation restoration) permits reversal of X, whereas reversing X first is strongly impaired in the tested AncGR2 backgrounds? Score reverse-path constraints separately from forward chronology; do not expand them into unmeasured pairwise mutation orders.
replication_targets.scope_note: W contains five substitutions and has no established internal chronological order. These additional assayed sites invalidate the earlier claim that order evidence covers only X/Y/Z. Forward W-completion constraints are recorded separately in SR5. At whole-block resolution, Fig4A supports restoring Y before W, and W before X; full W reversal is not necessary for every partial rescue.

replication_targets.finding: On the AncGR1.0 background used in Ortlund 2007, the complete group Y (L29M, F98I, S212del) abolishes activity unless both group X (S106P, L111Q) and group Z (N26T, Q105L) are present. X and Z may occur in either group-level order. The authors infer that X and Z preceded completion of Y along historically likely functional paths. This does not establish that every member of X or Z preceded every member of Y, or resolve the internal order of Y or Z. Y27R belongs to the earlier AncCR-to-AncGR1.0 branch and is permissive for the later XYZ phenotype.
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon place X and Z before completion of Y, allowing either order between X and Z, on the matching AncGR1.0 background? Compare Y27R using its earlier phylogenetic interval. Do not score unmeasured member-by-member precedence as ground truth.

assayed_genotypes._note: Ortlund Fig. 3A, all on the AncGR1 background. These are the measured intermediates behind the order constraint.
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1: functional, MR-like (responds to aldosterone, DOC, cortisol)
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+X: functional; preference switched toward cortisol, some MR-ligand sensitivity retained
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+Z: functional; little or no effect without Y
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+X+Y+Z: functional; fully GR-like, complete cortisol specificity
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+X+Z: functional; cortisol preference, not the fully cortisol-specific XYZ phenotype

replication_targets.scope_note: Ortlund 2007 assays seven later-branch events in X/Y/Z (six amino-acid substitutions and the S212 single-codon deletion) plus earlier Y27R. The full AncGR1.0-to-AncGR2 branch contains 36 amino-acid substitutions plus one deletion. Bridgham 2009 adds five assayed W substitutions. S212del has no homologous residue coordinate in modern human GR; score its ancestral/alignment column or indel unit and do not assign it to modern Asp742 or count its absence from a residue-only detector as a miss. These group-level assays do not determine every individual order.

replication_targets.finding: Restrictive group W (H84Q, Y91C, A107Y, G114Q, L197M) markedly reduces sensitivity in AncGR1.0 backgrounds lacking X, but weakly or moderately improves activation and cortisol specificity in X-containing backgrounds. The authors infer that W was unlikely to have been complete before the remodeling caused by X. At least some W events therefore likely followed the function switch; their individual order is unresolved.
replication_targets.source: Bridgham 2009, pp. 517-518, Fig. 4b and accompanying text
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon prefer X before completion of W in the matching AncGR1.0 forward benchmark? Do not require every W member to follow every X member.
replication_targets.evidence_status: group-level functional-path inference, not direct historical chronology

replication_targets.finding: In the updated AncCR-to-AncGR1.1 reconstruction of Carroll 2011, V43A and R116H are large-effect desensitizing substitutions. C71S alone has negligible effect on sensitivity, but buffers their double mutant to AncGR1.1-like sensitivity. Q113K also reduces sensitivity more weakly. The authors conjecture that C71S occurred before V43A and R116H; they do not directly determine chronological order.
replication_targets.test: Check recovery of V43A, R116H and buffering C71S on the exact2011 background. Report Q113K as weaker single-mutant phenotype evidence, not a demonstrated epistatic partner. Treat C71S-first as author conjecture, excluded from measured-order scoring.

order_expectation.evidence_status: author conjecture supported by buffering assays

replication_targets.scope_note: AncGR1.1 differs from the AncGR1.0 reconstruction used in 2007/2009. Do not concatenate their exact substitutions into one trajectory: position 107, for example, is S in AncGR1.1 but A in the AncGR1.0 background of W=A107Y. Stability effects in this paper are FoldX predictions, not measured thermal stability.

structures.notes: 7PRX is the wild-type modern human GR ligand-binding domain with numbering equal to UniProt P04150. Use it as a structural scaffold; its sequence and conformation are not the ancestral experimental background. The ancestral series is a backup. 3RY9 is the updated AncGR1.1 structure, not the AncGR1.0 reconstruction used in 2007/2009. Load data/numbering_offsets.json and the verified reference for the ancestral-to-modern crosswalk; the S212 deletion has no modern homologous residue and must not be assigned modern742.

known_limitations: The NR3C1 TOGA2 reference is the GR-gamma isoform: positions after 451 are one higher than UniProt / 7PRX numbering. Misapplying this shifts the entire ligand-binding domain by one residue, silently.
The Carroll 2011 stability table is calculated, not measured.
No cortisol-bound ancestral structure exists. 2Q1V is titled cortisol but its deposited ligand is prednisone.
No study determines a complete individual-substitution chronology. Score measured group-level functional constraints, preferred paths and author conjectures as separate evidence types.
The modern residue formerly assigned to S212del (Asp742) is not the deleted serine homolog. A source-anchored crosswalk is required at ancestral211/212.
The 2007/2009 AncGR1.0 and 2011 AncGR1.1 backgrounds are distinct reconstructions and require separate matched endpoints.
expected_outcome_note: This case provides experimentally supported partial order constraints at assayed group resolution, a preferred internal X path, and a separate 2011 conjecture about buffering-first order. It provides no unique total historical sequence. SR1/SR2/SR6 test sites, SR3/SR4/SR5 test applicable group-level or path constraints with matching reconstructed backgrounds.

substitution_sets._numbering: AncCR local LBD numbering as used in the original papers. Load data/numbering_offsets.json and the source-verified reference rather than hardcoding an offset. S212del is a deletion with no homologous modern residue; coordinate742 is a neighboring modern residue, not its substitution target.

adaptive_but_deleterious_group_Y.note: completes the switch structurally but destabilises the AF-H network; lethal without X and Z
adaptive_but_deleterious_group_Y.human_GR_note: S212del has no modern homologous residue. Record an indel unit and flanking coordinates using the source-anchored crosswalk, not a spurious Ser212-to-Asp742 substitution.

permissive_group_Z.human_GR_note: GR 557 is Trp in human GR, not the Thr of AncGR2's N26T -- human GR has diverged further at this site. GR 636 matches Q105L.

restrictive_group_W.note: Bridgham 2009 group W; internal order unresolved. X likely preceded completion of W; W reversal permits tested X reversal.

early_buffering_2011.note: Buffers V43A/R116H; preceding them is an author conjecture. Wild-type human GR carries Phe602, not this historical Ser state.

receptor_versions.AncCR: Ancestral corticoid receptor, ~450 Ma, MR-like: responds to aldosterone, DOC and cortisol. Carries ancestral Tyr27.
receptor_versions.AncGR1: AncGR1.0: the 2007/2009 GR-node reconstruction, still promiscuous in ligand specificity. Already carries Y27R. This is the background of X/Y/Z/W experiments.
receptor_versions.AncGR2: GR of the common ancestor of bony vertebrates; cortisol-specific. Carries X, Y and Z.
receptor_versions._intervals: 2007/2009: AncCR -> AncGR1.0, 25 substitutions; AncGR1.0 -> AncGR2, 36 amino-acid substitutions plus one single-codon deletion. 2011 updated reconstruction: AncCR -> AncGR1.1, 36 amino-acid differences.
receptor_versions._human_GR: 7PRX carries the derived states at Anc 27, 29, 98, 105, 106 and 111 (Arg558, Met560, Ile629, Leu636, Pro637, Gln642) but not at 26. Human GR is not AncGR2; use it as a scaffold, not as the derived genotype.
receptor_versions.AncGR1.1: Updated 2011 reconstruction of the same node using expanded cartilaginous-fish sampling; low hormone sensitivity. The 3RY9 structure is this reconstruction, and it must not silently replace AncGR1.0 in the earlier benchmark.
